# Page-relative local frame resizing

Original controls generated by `tools/relative_shape_frame_fixture.py` using
python-docx (MIT), lxml (BSD) and this repository's original drawing helpers.
The reference application exported the exact source read-only to
`controls-native.pdf`. No corpus XML, font binary or external renderer is bundled.

Twenty-three pages vary child rotation across 0°, 30°, 45°, 90°, 135°, 180°, 270° and
315°, with and without effect extents/physical 2pt pens. Additional cases cover
14pt Arial text, a pattern fill and nested group coordinates. The authored
120x240pt frame is sized to 40% of page width and 30% of page height, making the
order of nonuniform resizing and rotation observable. Compatibility mode is 15.

`tools/relative_shape_frame_reference.py` records visible green bounds at 96dpi,
native text runs and text ink bounds, and source/PDF/page raster hashes. The
browser tests compare all twenty-three shapes within 1pt, both text cases within
1pt, and exercise export/reopen and exact undo. Pixel-bound rounding accounts
for up to 0.75pt in the measured comparisons. Original sources pass eight XML
schema checks, including supported published drawing extensions.

The previous renderer stretched a completed bitmap to the relative frame.
Native controls instead require resizing local frames before rotation. This
is distinct from group-coordinate transforms: the group's existing quarter-
turn exchange of scale axes still applies to its own coordinate scale. Resize
the group coordinate extents with its frame to preserve that distinction.
Text, physical pens and source path coordinates retain their own units.

Cases 21–23 add nonuniform nested group coordinates and mismatched outer/group
extents, with both relative and fixed sizing. The reference application uses the root group's own
physical extent for geometry; a different saved `wp:extent` does not introduce
another geometry scale. The outer extent still supplies layout and the basis
for percentage resizing. These cases prevent conflating the two transforms.

The implementation uses a runtime scene copy; original OPC parts and scene
data remain intact. Unchanged frame/field/phase requests reuse the raster.
Changed requests close the previous bitmap only after the replacement passes
the session's existing 64-megapixel budget; a rejected replacement is closed
and the previous bitmap remains usable. A separate browser check verifies
this lifecycle and scene immutability.

Relevant definitions: ECMA-376 Part 1 §§20.4.2.3, 20.4.2.6–7 (anchor/effect
extents/frame), §§20.1.7.5–6 (group/shape transforms), and
[MS-ODRAWXML §5.11](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/office_standards/ms-odrawxml/1a38a99a-16ae-420d-8c79-23dc2e922717)
for `wp14:sizeRelH`/`sizeRelV`. The detailed ordering is native compatibility
evidence; it is not presented as an explicit formula in that extension schema.
